rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The IUCN Red List uses standardized categories (EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD, NE) to assess extinction risk. Understanding these categories is essential for prioritizing conservation action and policy.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Extinct means no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died.
Endangered means a very high risk of extinction in the wild in the near future.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ 'Threatened' is a single category. ✅ 'Threatened' collectively refers to CR, EN, and VU.  ·  ❌ Rare species are always endangered. ✅ Rarity alone doesn't imply endangerment; population trend matters.

rows.label: Special cases

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Q.** Define Extinct, Endangered, and Vulnerable per IUCN criteria. **Answer.** **Extinct (EX)** — no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died; exhaustive surveys in known and expected habitat, at appropriate times, have failed to record any.…  ·  **Q.** What is the difference between EW and EX? **Answer.** **EX (Extinct)** — the last individual has died anywhere; nothing survives in the wild **or** captivity. **EW (Extinct in the Wild)** — the species survives **only in captivity or cultivation**; its wild populations are gone.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Extinct, endangered, vulnerable, rare an  ·  Contrast  ·  Example  ·  Limit

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: IUCN Red List = global species conservation status inventory  ·  EX: no living individuals remain  ·  EW: survives only in captivity/cultivation  ·  CR, EN, VU = threatened categories (in decreasing severity)

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: IUCN Red List founded in 1964  ·  Over 150,000 species assessed

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **Q.** List the IUCN categories in order of decreasing extinction risk. **Answer.** **EX** (Extinct) → **EW** (Extinct in the Wild) → **CR** (Critically Endangered) → **EN** (Endangered) → **VU** (Vulnerable) → **NT** (Near Threatened) → **LC** (Least Concern).…  ·  **Q.** Why is 'Data Deficient' not the same as 'Least Concern'? **Answer.** **DD** means we simply **lack the data** to assess risk — the species may be common or may be slipping to extinction unnoticed; its status is unknown, not safe.…  ·  **Q.** Name three threatened species of Nepal and their IUCN status. **Answer.** 1. **Gharial** — Critically Endangered (CR), riverine specialist. 2. **Bengal florican** — Critically Endangered (CR), Terai grassland bird. 3.…

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Red panda — Endangered (EN)  ·  Snow leopard — Vulnerable (VU)

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A species with no living individual left is → C  ·  Endangered means → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The IUCN Red List is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species, maintained by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.  ·  Extinct (EX): no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died; no surveys can find it.  ·  Extinct in the Wild (EW): survives only in captivity or cultivation, with no natural population.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: NT: close to threatened  ·  LC: lowest risk  ·  DD: insufficient data; NE: not evaluated

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Extinct in the wild means extinct. ✅ EW species still survive in captivity.  ·  ❌ Data deficient means safe. ✅ DD means unknown risk, not low risk.  ·  Dodo — Extinct (EX)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Vulnerable means a high risk, but not as immediate as endangered.  ·  State the definition in one sentence, then give the example from the note. **Answer.** **Definition:** the IUCN Red List (founded 1964) is the global inventory that classifies each species' extinction risk into ordered categories.…  ·  Build the contrast the note uses. **Answer.** **Threatened vs not-threatened:** the note's contrast is between the three **threatened categories** (CR > EN > VU — risk of extinction is high now) and the **lower-risk categories** (NT — close to qualifying; LC — low risk).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Name one limit or cost. **Answer.** **Limit:** Red List categories are based on the **best available data**, and for many species the data are old, patchy or regional — so categories can lag reality in both directions (a recovering species stays listed; a quietly collapsing one stays LC/DD).…  ·  More than 42,000 species threatened with extinction  ·  Nepal has 27 mammal species listed as threatened

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Critically Endangered (CR): extremely high risk of extinction in the wild; e.g., population < 50 mature individuals or rapid decline.  ·  Endangered (EN): very high risk of extinction in the wild; smaller populations or steeper declines than CR threshold.  ·  Vulnerable (VU): high risk of extinction in the wild; larger populations than EN but still threatened.
